From: Anya Petrov <anya@clarityhealth.io>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in p95/p99 RTT for hosted API (clarity-prod)

Hi Jonas / Redwood ops,

We're seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 latencies on the hosted API in our production environment starting ~08:50 PDT. Error rate is stable but latency has doubled for tail latency and several of our critical endpoints are timing out. Our dashboards (attached screenshot) show the RTT distribution shifting to the right. This is customer-impacting — we're getting retries and user-visible slowdowns.

Can you confirm if any routing or region changes happened on your side? We did not change our traffic. Impact: several live users in west-US reported slow form submissions.

Requesting an initial triage and ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Anya Petrov
Head of Platform, Clarity Health
anya@clarityhealth.io

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in p95/p99 RTT for hosted API (clarity-prod)

Checked control plane & routing configs. Early findings: several egress BGP paths for our west-2 region began preferring a US-east peer due to an unexpected AS path change at 08:48. That increases RTT for west-US clients routed to east-US POPs.

Action taken so far:
- Pulled BGP visibility and trace logs (attached) — see egress-trace-clarity-20270921.log.
- Applied temporary local-preference override to steer traffic back to west-2 POPs (propagating now).
- Spun up additional short-lived capacity in west-2 to absorb the bump while we restore routing.

Next: confirm whether customer connections are reassigning to closer POPs, and watch p95 over the next 15-30 minutes. If we see persistent tail, we will fail traffic to the smaller quantized model variant to keep latency SLOs.

Lauren Bishop
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Recommended immediate customer message: acknowledge cause (cross-region egress path change), note mitigation applied, and offer a credit for user impact window (let sales/finance handle the amount).

Subject: Re: Sudden spike in p95/p99 RTT for hosted API (clarity-prod) — update

Hi Anya,

Thank you for the quick flag. Short update on our end: at ~08:48 PDT an upstream path change caused some west-US requests to be routed via a us-east egress peer, which added an extra inter-region hop and increased tail RTTs (p95/p99). Our SREs identified the AS-path anomaly, applied a local-preference override, and initiated controls to steer traffic back to west-2 POPs. We also temporarily increased west-2 capacity while the change propagated.

Current status: median latency is normal, p95 has improved ~30% and p99 is decreasing — we will continue to monitor for the next 2 hours. We apologize for the disruption; we understand the user impact and are opening a postmortem.

Next steps and asks:
- We will deliver a full postmortem within 72 hours that details the root cause and permanent mitigations (BGP guards, route monitoring, alerting).
- Our finance team will follow up on compensation. Vanessa (cc) will coordinate details.

If you can share any request IDs or user reports from 08:40–09:00 PDT that would help us validate the full scope.

Apologies again — we'll keep you updated.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
